name: Metchosin

facts.text: Metchosin's Tree Management Bylaw regulates tree removal because Council wants continuous tree cover kept; the District's tree cutting permit page is the starting point.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Cutting Permits - District of Metchosin
facts.excerpt: Council believes that maintaining continuous tree cover in Metchosin important to the community and the region
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: Local reporting says Metchosin's bylaw lets owners cut up to 10 trees per acre, that any tree on the protected list (featuring Garry oak) needs a permit, and that fines were raised to $10,000 per violation.
facts.sourceTitle: Metchosin tree fines spike - Goldstream Gazette
facts.excerpt: you can still cut down 10 trees per acre
facts.note: SECONDARY source (news/third-party), from search snippet; confirm with the municipality before publishing. Undated. Protected-species list at https://www.metchosin.ca/node/521 not read.

facts.text: Metchosin allows backyard burning of dry leaves, trimmings and yard debris from the same property only between 6 am and 6 pm. Debris over 10 cm needs a written permit from the Metchosin Fire Department, burning is limited to two days in a row on suitable venting days, and beach fires are prohibited.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Excerpt is snippet wording. Season (older reports: Oct 1 to May 31) not confirmed; Fire Dept 250-478-1307.

facts.text: Metchosin's development permit areas are the Village Centre, Shoreline Slopes and Bilston Floodplain, so waterfront-bluff and Bilston Creek floodplain lots need a check before land alteration.
facts.excerpt: include the Village Centre Development Permit Area, Shoreline Slopes Development Permit Area, Bilston Floodplain Development Permit Area
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. The OCP (Bylaw 258, consolidated Apr 2025) also lists a Centre Mountain DPA; the web page may be out of date.

facts.text: Metchosin's OCP gives Council responsibility for the sensitive areas on Map 4 and for unmapped sensitive areas, with riparian policies in section 2.3.9 ('Sensitive Environments in Metchosin').
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Advisory Select Committee agenda package, Nov 26 2024 (District of Metchosin)
facts.excerpt: Council has responsibility for the sensitive area indicated on Map 4 and other sensitive areas not specifically shown on that map
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: Metchosin has 1,658 ha (4,211 acres) in the Agricultural Land Reserve plus many large rural properties, so work here is often on farm edges, hedgerows, pasture and acreage.
facts.excerpt: 1,658 ha (4,211 acres) of land in the Agricultural Land Reserve

facts.text: Many Metchosin properties rely on wells drawing on Aquifer 606, though parts of the District are on CRD piped water; well owners are responsible for testing and maintenance.
facts.sourceTitle: Aquifers of the Capital Regional District (Province of B.C.)
facts.excerpt: there is thought to be a greater reliance upon wells for domestic water sources in Sooke, Metchosin, and the Western Communities
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm. Many Metchosin properties are on wells; the rules apply only where connected.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Dates and day split also shown in the Saanich watering-schedules page snippet. Shared regional block, not municipality-specific.

facts.text: Under B.C.'s Riparian Areas Protection Regulation, the assessment area for a stream is a 30 m strip on each side measured from the high water mark; where a local government applies it, work in that strip can need a Qualified Environmental Professional's report.
facts.sourceTitle: Riparian Areas Protection Regulation (RAPR) - Province of B.C.
facts.excerpt: The former Riparian Areas Regulation was amended on November 1, 2019 and became the Riparian Areas Protection Regulation.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Provincial rule: shared regional block.

facts.text: B.C.'s Wildlife Act (section 34) protects occupied bird nests, and eagle, osprey, heron and some other nests year-round, so trees are checked for active nests before felling or heavy pruning, especially in spring and summer.
facts.sourceTitle: Wildlife - Environmental regulatory compliance (Province of B.C.)
facts.excerpt: The protection for eagle and heron nests applies even outside of the breeding season.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Provincial rule: shared regional block.
